issues.description: Class PersonResource constructor: the template declares a constructor that accepts a PersonService parameter (public PersonResource(PersonService personService)) to enable Spring dependency injection into the REST resource. The solution repository's PersonResource declares a constructor that accepts a String parameter (public PersonResource(String personService)) and assigns it to the PersonService field. This type mismatch prevents correct dependency injection and will cause a compilation error or runtime wiring failure, and therefore will confuse or block students trying to understand or run the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java (solution) to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the existing field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure the constructor parameter type matches the declared field so Spring can perform dependency injection and the code compiles.
